titre.sous: She said that ... He told me that ...

bulles.texte: She said the meeting **was** on Monday.

temps.titre: From the speaker to the reporter

lignes.exemple: He said he was busy **that day**.

options.texte: He said he **would send** it **the next day**.
options.raison: will, would. tomorrow, the next day

etapes.texte: In reported speech, the verb **moves back**: will, would
The right answer __rephrases__ the message, without the exact words

phrases.texte: When we report what someone said, the verb moves one step into the past. Is becomes was.
phrases.dit: When we report what someone said, the verb moves one step into the past. Is, becomes was.

phrases.texte: Will becomes would. Can becomes could.
phrases.dit: Will, becomes would. Can, becomes could.

phrases.texte: And the simple past becomes the past perfect: she said she had sent it.
Time words change too. Today becomes that day. Tomorrow becomes the next day. Yesterday becomes the day before.
phrases.dit: Time words change too. Today, becomes that day. Tomorrow, becomes the next day. Yesterday, becomes the day before.

phrases.texte: One trap: say or tell? She said me the news is wrong.
phrases.dit: One trap: say, or tell? She said me the news, is wrong.

phrases.texte: Tell takes a person: she told me the news. Say takes the words: she said she was late.
phrases.dit: Tell, takes a person: she told me the news. Say, takes the words: she said she was late.

phrases.texte: Now, a TOEIC question from Part 4. You hear a message: I will send the contract tomorrow.
phrases.dit: Now, a TOEIC question from Part four. You hear a message: I will send the contract tomorrow.

phrases.texte: What does the speaker say? A: He sent the contract yesterday. B: He said he would send it the next day.
phrases.dit: What does the speaker say? Answer A. He sent the contract yesterday. Answer B. He said he would send it the next day.

phrases.texte: C: He will sign the contract. D: He cannot send the contract.
phrases.dit: Answer C. He will sign the contract. Answer D. He cannot send the contract.

phrases.texte: A is in the past, but the contract is not sent yet. C changes send into sign. D says the opposite.
phrases.dit: A is in the past, but the contract is not sent yet. C changes send, into sign. D says the opposite.

phrases.texte: B is correct. Will becomes would, and tomorrow becomes the next day.
phrases.dit: B is correct. Will, becomes would, and tomorrow, becomes the next day.

phrases.texte: Three steps. One: in reported speech, the verb moves back.
Two: say takes the words, tell takes a person.
phrases.dit: Two: say, takes the words. Tell, takes a person.

phrases.texte: Three: the right answer rephrases the message, without the exact words.
